title: Reinforcement-learning-guided CdS shell-growth route using AlphaFlow
summary: AlphaFlow used reinforcement learning with an automated droplet reactor to select and optimize reagent sequences for CdS-shell growth on supplied CdSe quantum dots. Under the authors’ aged, diluted starting-material comparison, the selected route achieved a 26 nm larger absorption-peak shift and 450% higher photoluminescence intensity after six cycles than the conventional sequence; freshly diluted starting material showed a different comparison. This is a lab route to a known nanomaterial, not discovery of a new compound or proof of universal superiority.
ai_technology: Reinforcement-learning agent with neural reward regression and boosted-tree viability classification in an automated fluidic lab
organization: North Carolina State University; University at Buffalo

evidence.tested: Primary Nature Communications article reports a six-cycle experimental comparison on aged diluted starting material; conditions and starting materials constrain result.
evidence.unknown: Earlier route disclosures and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement-learning-guided reaction sequence selection and optimization linked to measured shell-growth signals.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text checked for identity, dates, organization affiliations, AI method and bounded experimental comparison.
